records.supports: Daijisen on noun is printing block. Seisenban native noun identifies Japanese cherry birch, preserves historical alternate tree identifications, wood-for-bows, abbreviated bow/medium, Noh accompaniment and printing-block senses. Separate on heading identifies Chinese catalpa reference and block/publication uses. Jitsu confirms on/kun, but its broader historical/structural discussion is not copied into teaching.
records.qualification: Do not universally equate native azusa with catalpa or silently restrict unrestricted JMdict printing-block sense to shi. Dictionaries' different botanical layers and historical uses are distinguished, not forced into one species. Botanical current naming in this lesson is source-qualified, not independent modern taxonomy certification.

records.supports: Daijisen explicitly assigns kitsu to citrus compounds including kankitsurui, alongside plant/clan senses. Seisenban distinguishes older edible mandarin naming from modern wild evergreen tachibana; gives white flowers, bitter/sour fruit, ornamental planting, alternative plant name, blossom, crest, fragrant-wood/blended-fragrance and place/name uses. Family-name heading separate. Later geographic/encyclopedia sections were not used as plant evidence.
records.qualification: Modern chosen plant sense does not erase older edible-citrus senses, blossoms or specialist historical naming. No instruction to eat bitter fruit, no name-course expansion, no invented universal substitution or frequency claim.
